newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco smoke harms children - environment meet.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco smoke harms children - environment meet.

text.p: Tobacco smoke poses a significant health risk to children, weakening their lungs and provoking respiratory disorders, international environmental officials said on Tuesday at a meeting attended by officials from "G-7" countries as well as Russia, the EU and the United Nations.

"We affirm that environmental tobacco smoke is a significant public health risk to young children and that parents need to know about the risks of smoking in the home around their young children," said a declaration issued at the end of a two-day meeting chaired by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency chief Carol Browner.
"Children exposed to environmental tobacco smoke are more likely to suffer from reduced lung function, lower respiratory tract infections and respitory irritaions."
Children with asthma were especially at risk, it said, adding that these symptons lea to increased hospitalisations of children.
Their remarks come ahead of a landmark trial in Miami concerning the effects of second-smoke.

The case, known as Norma Broin et al vs. Philip Morris Cos. Inc et al, is filed on behalf of an estimated 60,000 non-smoking flight attentants suffering from lung diseases and other ailments allegedly caused by second-hand smoke on U.S. passenger jets.
The trial, the first of a class-action lawsuit against cigarette makers, is due to begin on June 2.
